dimensions.explanation: The reading concerns post-authorisation material changes to an investment objective, policy or restriction of a covered UCITS fund. These are alternative categories of change; all three need not change simultaneously. Initial authorisation and operator changes are separate matters.

Covered funds are UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands, and UK-domiciled collective investment schemes authorised as UK UCITS. Materiality, novelty, complexity and potential local policy implications remain undefined. Local policy is interpreted as Hong Kong policy. Applying these terms requires judgment and potentially implementing guidance.

Home-jurisdiction compliance is a positive condition of relief. Novel product features, complex product features or possible local policy implications each independently exclude relief; actual policy harm need not be established. Pre-commencement pending applications remain under the existing process even where the substantive change would otherwise qualify.

The measure conditionally removes the SFC's prior-approval requirement. Exceptions preserve the otherwise applicable requirement rather than create a blanket prohibition. Home compliance does not necessarily mean home-regulator approval; the source does not prescribe that equivalence. Notification requirements remain relevant. The SFC will continue post-vetting and may make enquiries or take appropriate regulatory action for non-compliance.

The express effective date, 2025-11-28, governs the introductory reference to immediate effect. The transition is interpreted as testing outstanding approval or authorisation at commencement, although the assessment time is not expressly stated. SFC receipt before that date, rather than submission alone, is specified. Receipt on that date is not receipt before it. Withdrawal, refiling and modification of pending applications remain unaddressed.

Earlier uncertainty remains concerning applicable home requirements, the existing approval process, implementing FAQs, forms and checklists, and case-specific fund, change and application facts. citations.quote: Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.

For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.
The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC.

readings.statement: From 2025-11-28, this circular removes prior SFC approval for a covered UCITS fund's post-authorisation material change to an investment objective, policy or restriction if the change complies with home-jurisdiction requirements, involves neither novel nor complex product features, and has no potential local policy implications, subject to the application transition. Covered funds are UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands, and UK-domiciled collective investment schemes authorised as UK UCITS. Novelty, complexity or possible Hong Kong policy implications each excludes relief; failure to satisfy home requirements likewise leaves the otherwise applicable approval requirement in place. Home compliance must be established under the applicable home rules, not assumed from home supervision alone. If the SFC received an application before 2025-11-28 and approval or authorisation remained outstanding at commencement, the SFC continues processing it under the existing process even if the change would otherwise qualify for relief. This does not itself establish the outcome of that process or automatically dispose of the application. Management companies remain subject to applicable notification and filing requirements, whose full content is not supplied. The SFC continues post-vetting and may make follow-up enquiries or take regulatory action for non-compliance. The particular approval outcome for an excluded or transitional case remains dependent on the existing rules and missing implementing materials.
